capture_method: Running fleet TUI in a 116x38 tmux pane; capture-pane -p -e parsed with pyte and rendered to PNG using Pillow and DejaVu Sans Mono. Matching plain terminal captures accompany every PNG. No mocked TUI model or generated UI images.
fixture: Isolated fleetd state; real Debian container running the generated AudioScript(false, true) as fleetuser; two real output client processes named laptop and studio. Devices are private PulseAudio null sinks, not physical speakers. laptop uses the local Unix socket; studio was also exercised over fleetd's authenticated loopback TCP listener used by SSH remote access.
audio_path: paplay in container -> fleetoutput.monitor -> fleet output source via docker exec -> fleetd Output gRPC -> output.Run -> paplay on selected client -> monitored client sink

signal.measurement: Each probe records two seconds and analyzes the final one second (48000 samples from one stereo channel). Frequency is estimated by positive-going zero crossings.

limits: Linux virtual audio endpoints; no physical speaker/headphone listening test.
macOS arm64 cross-build and device-parser tests passed; CoreAudio playback not run on hardware.
Authenticated loopback TCP tested; external SSH forwarding and gateway network traversal not exercised.
Coder and Codespaces output backends are unsupported, matching current microphone support.
review_regressions: Unrelated standby connections preserve pinned playback.
Requested devices survive fallback and return on refreshed enumeration.
A client losing all playback devices releases Auto selection.
Revision-ordered Watch updates cannot undo newer rapid local selector changes.
Queued samples drain at end of a source.

validation.command: buf lint fleetgrpc && buf build fleetgrpc
